name: Simon
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: Before this there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, and they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. History outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks, became known as the father of heretics, taught salvation by grace alone without works, and finally fell to his death when Peter commanded the demons carrying him to release him; the validity of that account is uncertain, but it shows Simon was a sorcerer deceiving the people.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money: a carnal minded man. Or you come into this truth saying, I want to be a captain, I want to be the deacon, I want to be the bishop.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands he may receive the Holy Ghost. Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory; he had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have.
